data.why: The repo ships example/example_fig.csv (prediction coordinates/logits/metadata) paired with example/example_sounds.wav, which the CSV references by its repo-relative path 'example/example_sounds.wav'; that WAV stays in place in /work/app and the CSV is handed to the browser to upload via the dcc.Upload control on the TrillView page.

goals: Load a CSV of model prediction coordinates and confidence scores to see the radial spatial distribution of species classification confidence
Hover over points in the scatterplot to inspect the spectrogram and listen to the underlying audio frame for a given prediction
Select a cluster of points (e.g. an outlier region or a specific species group) and save them to a CSV subset for closer review
Open the saved subset in Spec View to page through spectrograms, re-label individual frames, and export corrected labels
Compare predicted vs. actual species labels and prediction scores to diagnose misclassifications or anomalous confidence patterns

review.summary: The tree follows the documented route through the interface (load predictions, explore the radial plot with hover and click previews, box-select and save a subset, then page through and relabel it in Spec View), and the 11 screens I checked match their nodes. Before filing, it needs an explicit task for reading the radial layout to assess performance and find anomalies, which is the paper's main purpose, and the unsupported 'edited cards are highlighted' claim removed from f4.
